# Release check: 2026-11-27, before v1.1.0

A fresh agent with no context followed only the README, using the public Swagger Petstore spec. Its findings, most serious first, and what happened to each:

| Finding | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Frontmatter, OpenAPI and version checks ignored the user's folder and reported this repository's counts | Fixed: `npm run validate:docs` runs every check on the user's docs and names what it checked (PR 10) |
| `validate:quality` passed docs with broken frontmatter | Fixed: `validate:docs` includes the frontmatter check (PR 10) |
| CI for a bootstrapped docs repo could not be set up | Fixed: the bootstrap writes a working CI workflow (PR 10) |
| Generated docs added a Bearer token with no security defined, dropped `allOf` fields, contradicted themselves on required fields, and invented a 204 body | Fixed (PR 10) |
| Export writes into the toolkit and uploads nothing; PDF output is plain text | Documented in the README; export marked as lighter-tested (PR 11) |
| `proof:path` generates inside the toolkit | Documented accurately in the README (PR 11) |
| Bootstrapped CODEOWNERS assigned every path to the toolkit's author | Fixed: commented example rules only (PR 10) |
| `lint:markdown` crashes on paths outside the repository | Deferred |

Later testing against five OpenAPI Initiative example specs (now in `tests/fixtures/third-party/`) found three more generator problems, fixed with the adopter tests: server variables left unresolved in URLs, form-encoded request bodies reported as "Not applicable", and named response examples ignored.
